sn18.1:1.3: Rāhula was the Buddha’s son to his wife, who is often known as Yasodharā. Rāhula’s going forth is related at [pli-tv-kd1:54.1.1](), and other important discourses with him include [mn61](), [mn62](), and [mn147]() = [sn35.121](), in which he became an arahant. The Buddha declared him the foremost of monks who desire training ([an1.209]()). His name is often explained as meaning “attachment”, but it probably refers rather to being born under the influence of the dark star Rāhu ([sn2.8]()).
sn18.1:4.1: In this and similar passages, Mahāsaṅgīti edition inserts unnecessary ellipses.
